tasks.task_name: Create user stories and acceptance criteria for MVP
tasks.description:
Develop comprehensive user stories and acceptance criteria for the CLI tool MVP as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (Section 6.2.1).

This is one of the four critical MVP deliverables that the Product Manager must produce. User stories define the functional requirements from the user's perspective, while acceptance criteria provide the testable conditions that must be met for each story to be considered complete.

This artifact will serve as the primary input for development work and will be used by:
- Backend/CLI Developers to understand what features to implement
- Quality Assurance to create test plans and validate functionality
- Technical Lead to make architectural decisions based on functional requirements
- Stakeholders to understand and approve the MVP scope

The user stories should follow standard formats (e.g., 'As a [user type], I want [goal] so that [benefit]') and each should have clear, measurable acceptance criteria.
tasks.task_notes: This is marked as priority 1 because user stories and acceptance criteria are foundational artifacts that other development tasks will depend on. Without these, the development team cannot proceed with implementation. The quality and completeness of these artifacts will directly impact the success of the MVP delivery.

tasks.task_name: Define MVP scope for CLI tool
tasks.description:
Create a comprehensive MVP scope definition document that clearly delineates what features and functionality will be included in the minimum viable product release of the CLI tool, as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (Section 6.2.1).

This is one of the four critical MVP deliverables. The MVP scope definition serves as the boundary document that:
- Identifies features that are IN scope for the MVP release
- Explicitly calls out features that are OUT of scope (deferred to post-MVP)
- Defines the success criteria for the MVP as a whole
- Provides justification for scope decisions based on user value and technical feasibility
- Sets expectations with stakeholders on what will be delivered

Given the context mentions a CLI tool with Notion API integration, the scope definition should address core functionality related to these components while maintaining a realistic MVP boundary.
tasks.task_notes: This is priority 1 because scope definition is essential before detailed implementation planning can occur. Without a clear MVP scope, there's risk of scope creep or misalignment between stakeholders and the development team. This document should be created early and referenced throughout development to ensure the team stays focused on MVP delivery.

tasks.task_name: Develop user testing plan for MVP

- Testing methodology (e.g., moderated vs. unmoderated, remote vs. in-person)
- Test scenarios and tasks for users to complete

The testing plan ensures that the MVP is validated against actual user needs and that any critical usability or functionality issues are identified and addressed before broader release.

The plan should be realistic for the team size (no dedicated UX researcher, so PM likely conducts testing). Consider whether beta testing or pilot programs are appropriate for a CLI tool.
